calibration.note: Brier score and expected calibration error are computed on cross-validated training predictions. Platt scaling (sigmoid) and isotonic regression were both fitted inside CV. The variant with the lowest Brier score is 'raw'; a margin of 0.002 is required before replacing the simpler uncalibrated model.

Logistic Regression.notes: Regularised linear baseline; coefficients are directly readable.

SVM (Linear).notes: Maximum-margin linear separator; scaling is mandatory. Probabilities come from Platt scaling on internal folds.

SVM (RBF).notes: Non-linear kernel; C and gamma jointly control the margin. Probabilities come from Platt scaling on internal folds.

Random Forest.notes: Bagged trees; depth and leaf size are the main brakes on overfitting at n=303.

XGBoost.notes: Gradient-boosted trees with L2 regularisation; shallow depth (2-4) suits a small tabular dataset.

selection.rule: 1. Rank by mean cross-validated ROC-AUC on the training split and keep every model within one standard error of the best; at 242 training rows, differences smaller than that are not real. 2. Apply the same one-standard-error filter to PR-AUC, so a model that is clearly weaker on the positive class is dropped. 3. Among the survivors prefer the better-calibrated model, treating Brier differences below 0.01 as ties. 4. Break remaining ties on interpretability - a clinical screening aid has to be explainable - then on the train/test gap, then on fit cost.

imbalance_study.stratification: StratifiedKFold / stratified train-test split used everywhere.
imbalance_study.decision: Training split is only mildly imbalanced (1.18:1, minority 45.9%). SMOTE was evaluated inside the CV folds (never on the whole dataset) and is reported above; it is not used in the final model because it did not improve cross-validated ROC-AUC over stratified sampling, and synthesising patients adds risk without solving a problem this dataset has. Class weighting remains a tunable option in every model's search grid.

early_stopping.note: Early stopping was run on an inner 80/20 split of the training data to find how many boosting rounds this dataset supports before validation loss stops improving. The result informed the small n_estimators values in the tuning grid; the grid search itself uses plain cross-validation so that every candidate is scored the same way.

patterns: Mean distance from the 0.38 threshold is 0.199 for wrong predictions versus 0.401 for correct ones - the model is measurably less certain when it errs.
1 false negatives: mean age 60.0, mean vessels coloured 0.00, mean ST depression 3.00 mm (test-set averages: 54.0, 0.93, 1.20).
10 false positives: mean age 55.8, mean vessels coloured 0.89, mean ST depression 0.69 mm (test-set averages: 54.0, 0.93, 1.20).
error_analysis.cost_note: A false negative sends a patient with significant narrowing away without follow-up; a false positive sends a healthy patient to further, sometimes invasive, testing. In screening the first error is normally the more serious one, which is why the operating threshold below is chosen to favour sensitivity rather than left at 0.5.

explainability.coefficient_note: Numeric features are standardised before fitting, so coefficients are comparable across features. An odds ratio above 1 means the model raises its estimated odds as that encoded feature increases.
explainability.permutation_note: Permutation importance shuffles one raw input column of the held-out test set and measures how much test ROC-AUC drops. A larger drop means the model leaned on that column more.

shap_summary.note: Mean absolute SHAP value per feature across the training split, in log-odds units. It measures how much each input moves this model's output, not medical causation.

class_balance.reading: Near balanced (1.18:1). Heavy re-sampling such as SMOTE is not indicated; stratified splits plus optional class weights are enough.
